label: third input token, right after an h in position 1
explanation: Fires at step t=2 (the third original token) when the previous input (original token 1) was h, whatever token is input at t=2. 99.5% of activation mass is at t=2. Strongest (about 1.0 of max) for i h h; typical values are about 0.5-0.9 of max. Weak residual activations: at t=1 when the first token is h (about 0.04), and at t=3 after an h at t=2 (about 0.05-0.1). Some false positives and very weak activations come with certain first tokens (v h ..., c h ...). It never fires in the delimiter or copy phase, and not after h at later positions.

issues: Main claims check out. 99.5% of activation mass is at t=2 and prev_tok is h on 100% of active steps. The feature never fires in the delimiter or copy phase (0 active steps), and never fires at t>=4. Test scores reproduce: P 0.974, R 0.954, F1 0.964, mass recall 0.994.

Residuals match the explanation. At t=1 with an h input there are about 559 dev actives at about 0.04 of max; (t==1)&(prev_tok==h) has precision 0.035 and mass 0.3%, which is consistent with the claim even though that predicate doesn't capture it exactly. The t=3-after-h residual has precision 0.013 and mass 0.25%, also weak, as claimed.

False positives are systematic but already disclosed. Predicate hits with first token c have precision 0.52 and those with first token v have 0.80; together they make up most of the 439 test FPs. Excluding both raises precision to 0.997 but lowers F1 to 0.952 (recall drops to 0.910), so it is not a better predicate.

The magnitude explanation understates how much the first token matters. With similar active counts (about 590-720 dev steps each), mass share varies about 6x: first token t gives 0.011, 3 gives 0.013 and e gives 0.018, against i 0.065, p 0.061 and a 0.054. So 'typical 0.5-0.9 of max' does not hold for those first tokens. This only affects magnitude, not where the feature fires, so it is not a refutation.
The test-split misses are almost all the weak t=1 h-at-position-0 activations (0.04) and hold only 0.6% of the mass. No missed-activation class with real mass remains.
